# Wander tools

Write, check, test, graph and inspect Wander behaviors.

9 tools in the `wander` category. Badges: **read-only** tools never change the project; **mutating** tools are undoable and attributed; **open-world** tools reach outside the engine and MCP clients ask before running them.

| Tool | Summary |
|---|---|
| [`wander_reference`](#wander_reference) | The Wander 2 guide for writing behaviors: syntax, triggers, statements, idioms, and every builtin function with its signature (generated from the builtin registry, including subsystem and native-module builtins). |
| [`wander_check`](#wander_check) | Compile Wander source without attaching it, exactly as the engine would run it (components, builtins, `use`d modules from the project). |
| [`behavior_set`](#behavior_set) | Create or replace a named behavior on an entity: its natural-language `intent` (the human source of truth), an optional structured `spec` derived from the intent ({summary, rules: [{text, tests: [test names]}]}), and the Wander `source`. |
| [`behavior_remove`](#behavior_remove) | Remove a named behavior from an entity. |
| [`behavior_spec`](#behavior_spec) | The intent -&gt; spec -&gt; code view of a behavior: its intent, the stored spec (rules an agent derived from the intent, each naming the tests that verify it), what the code declares (triggers, states, tunable params with ranges and current per-entity values, vars, functions, tests), and coverage (rules without tests, tests without rules). |
| [`wander_test`](#wander_test) | Run the `test "..."` blocks of a behavior in a sandbox simulation (the real scene is never touched): each test gets a fresh world, ticks once (on start ran), then runs with self = the entity under test; `wait` advances the simulation at 1/60 s, `emit`/`press`/`hold`/`release`/`click` inject input, and `expect` reports failures with the compared values. |
| [`behavior_graph`](#behavior_graph) | Visual node graph of a behavior (or raw `source`): bodies (handlers, fns, tests, state handlers) with an entry node, exec-flow statement nodes wired by exec pins (if: then/elif/else; loops: body), expression nodes wired into data pins, and literals/names inline on pins (`value`). |
| [`behavior_from_graph`](#behavior_from_graph) | Turn a node graph (from behavior_graph, possibly edited) back into Wander source. |
| [`wander_inspect`](#wander_inspect) | While playing: the runtime state of an entity's behaviors — current state of each state machine and how long it has been active, handlers waiting in `wait` (and for how long), plus the entity's vars. |

### `wander_reference` { #wander_reference }

**Wander language reference** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

The Wander 2 guide for writing behaviors: syntax, triggers, statements, idioms, and every builtin function with its signature (generated from the builtin registry, including subsystem and native-module builtins). Read it once before writing behaviors. topic="<category or function>" returns detailed entries with parameter types and examples, e.g. topic="physics", topic="list", topic="raycast".

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `topic` | string |  | Optional: a builtin category (math, vector, scene, list, physics...) or a function name |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    wander_reference {"topic": "physics"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call wander_reference '{"topic": "physics"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "wander_reference",
        "arguments": {
          "topic": "physics"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `wander_check` { #wander_check }

**Check Wander code** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

Compile Wander source without attaching it, exactly as the engine would run it (components, builtins, `use`d modules from the project). Returns diagnostics (line, column, stable code, message, did-you-mean hint, file for module errors), warnings, and a summary of the behaviors (vars, params, handlers, states, tests). format=true also returns the canonical formatting; disassemble=true the bytecode listing.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes | Wander source code |  |
| `format` | boolean |  | Also return the canonically formatted source |  |
| `disassemble` | boolean |  | Also return the bytecode listing (performance work) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    wander_check {"source": "behavior Coin\n  param spin = 90 in 0..360 \"degrees per second\"\n  on tick\n    rotate self by (0, spin * dt, 0)\n  end\n  test \"spins\"\n    let before = self.rotation.y\n    wait 0.5\n    expect self.rotation.y != before\n  end\nend", "format": true}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call wander_check '{"source": "behavior Coin\n  param spin = 90 in 0..360 \"degrees per second\"\n  on tick\n    rotate self by (0, spin * dt, 0)\n  end\n  test \"spins\"\n    let before = self.rotation.y\n    wait 0.5\n    expect self.rotation.y != before\n  end\nend", "format": true}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "wander_check",
        "arguments": {
          "source": "behavior Coin\n  param spin = 90 in 0..360 \"degrees per second\"\n  on tick\n    rotate self by (0, spin * dt, 0)\n  end\n  test \"spins\"\n    let before = self.rotation.y\n    wait 0.5\n    expect self.rotation.y != before\n  end\nend",
          "format": true
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `behavior_set` { #behavior_set }

**Set behavior** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Create or replace a named behavior on an entity: its natural-language `intent` (the human source of truth), an optional structured `spec` derived from the intent ({summary, rules: [{text, tests: [test names]}]}), and the Wander `source`. The source is compiled; by default code with errors is rejected and the diagnostics returned so you can fix and retry. Workflow: intent -> spec rules -> code with a `test` block per rule -> wander_test -> behavior_spec to check coverage.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | integer \| string | yes | Entity id (number) or exact name |  |
| `name` | string | yes | Behavior name, e.g. "Patrol" |  |
| `intent` | string |  | What the behavior should do, in plain language |  |
| `spec` | object |  | Structured spec: {summary, rules: [{text, tests: [...]}], notes} |  |
| `source` | string |  | Wander source code |  |
| `enabled` | boolean |  | Enabled (default true) |  |
| `allow_errors` | boolean |  | Save even if the code does not compile (default false) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    behavior_set {"entity": "Menu", "name": "Menu", "intent": "Play hides the menu", "source": "behavior Menu\n  on ui \"Play\"\n    self.enabled = false\n  end\nend"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call behavior_set '{"entity": "Menu", "name": "Menu", "intent": "Play hides the menu", "source": "behavior Menu\n  on ui \"Play\"\n    self.enabled = false\n  end\nend"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "behavior_set",
        "arguments": {
          "entity": "Menu",
          "name": "Menu",
          "intent": "Play hides the menu",
          "source": "behavior Menu\n  on ui \"Play\"\n    self.enabled = false\n  end\nend"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `behavior_spec` { #behavior_spec }

**Behavior spec** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

The intent -> spec -> code view of a behavior: its intent, the stored spec (rules an agent derived from the intent, each naming the tests that verify it), what the code declares (triggers, states, tunable params with ranges and current per-entity values, vars, functions, tests), and coverage (rules without tests, tests without rules). Use it to keep intent, spec and code in sync.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | integer \| string | yes | Entity id (number) or exact name |  |
| `name` | string | yes | Behavior name |  |


    ```bash
    skywalker call behavior_spec '{"entity": "Coin", "name": "Coin"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "behavior_spec",
        "arguments": {
          "entity": "Coin",
    ```

### `wander_test` { #wander_test }

**Run behavior tests** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

Run the `test "..."` blocks of a behavior in a sandbox simulation (the real scene is never touched): each test gets a fresh world, ticks once (on start ran), then runs with self = the entity under test; `wait` advances the simulation at 1/60 s, `emit`/`press`/`hold`/`release`/`click` inject input, and `expect` reports failures with the compared values. Pass entity+name (mode "entity" copies that entity's components, tags and vars; "scene" runs inside a copy of the whole scene; "isolated" uses a plain entity) or raw `source`. Returns pass/fail per test, failures with line numbers, logs and simulated time.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | integer \| string |  | Entity whose behavior to test |  |
| `name` | string |  | Behavior name |  |
| `source` | string |  | Test this source instead of a saved behavior |  |
| `filter` | string |  | Only tests whose name contains this |  |
| `mode` | string |  | Sandbox contents (default: entity) | `entity` `scene` `isolated` |
| `max_seconds` | number |  | Simulated time limit per test (default 600) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    wander_test {"entity": "Coin", "name": "Coin", "mode": "entity"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call wander_test '{"entity": "Coin", "name": "Coin", "mode": "entity"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "wander_test",
        "arguments": {
          "entity": "Coin",
          "name": "Coin",
          "mode": "entity"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `behavior_graph` { #behavior_graph }

**Behavior as a node graph** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

Visual node graph of a behavior (or raw `source`): bodies (handlers, fns, tests, state handlers) with an entry node, exec-flow statement nodes wired by exec pins (if: then/elif/else; loops: body), expression nodes wired into data pins, and literals/names inline on pins (`value`). Positions come from the saved layout or an automatic layout. Edit the JSON and send it back with behavior_from_graph. palette=true adds every node type with its pins.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | integer \| string |  | Entity id (number) or exact name |  |
| `name` | string |  | Behavior name |  |
| `source` | string |  | Graph this source instead |  |
| `palette` | boolean |  | Include the node palette |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    behavior_graph {"entity": "Coin", "name": "Coin"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call behavior_graph '{"entity": "Coin", "name": "Coin"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "behavior_graph",
        "arguments": {
          "entity": "Coin",
          "name": "Coin"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `behavior_from_graph` { #behavior_from_graph }

**Behavior from a node graph** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Turn a node graph (from behavior_graph, possibly edited) back into Wander source. With entity+name the code is compiled and saved as that behavior (rejected on errors unless allow_errors) and the node positions are stored, so the editor reopens the same layout. Returns the generated source and diagnostics.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `graph` | object | yes | Graph JSON (format wander-graph) |  |
| `entity` | integer \| string |  | Entity id (number) or exact name |  |
| `name` | string |  | Behavior name to save into |  |
| `allow_errors` | boolean |  | Save even if the code does not compile |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    behavior_from_graph {"entity": "Coin", "name": "Spin", "graph": {"format": "wander-graph", "version": 1, "behaviors": []}}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call behavior_from_graph '{"entity": "Coin", "name": "Spin", "graph": {"format": "wander-graph", "version": 1, "behaviors": []}}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "behavior_from_graph",
        "arguments": {
          "entity": "Coin",
          "name": "Spin",
          "graph": {
            "format": "wander-graph",
            "version": 1,
            "behaviors": []
          }
        }
      }
    }
    ```

<small>Pass the whole graph object that behavior_graph returned, after editing it; an empty graph like this one saves an empty behavior.</small>

### `wander_inspect` { #wander_inspect }

**Inspect running behaviors** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

While playing: the runtime state of an entity's behaviors — current state of each state machine and how long it has been active, handlers waiting in `wait` (and for how long), plus the entity's vars. Use it to debug why a behavior is not doing what its intent says.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | integer \| string | yes | Entity id (number) or exact name |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    wander_inspect {"entity": "Guard"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call wander_inspect '{"entity": "Guard"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "wander_inspect",
        "arguments": {
          "entity": "Guard"
        }
      }
    }
    ```
